3e5f14c8-bdfd-49a9-b77b-9d75454f678b.title: Anime Review: Yomi no Tsugai (Daemons of the Shadow Realm)
3e5f14c8-bdfd-49a9-b77b-9d75454f678b.incipit: Hiromu Arakawa is one of the legendary mangakas of our time. If you don’t know, she did Fullmetal Alchemist, Silver Spoon, and The Heroic Legend of Arslan... all of which received anime adaptations. Now, her...
3e5f14c8-bdfd-49a9-b77b-9d75454f678b.body:
Hiromu Arakawa is one of the legendary mangakas of our time. If you don’t know, she did Fullmetal Alchemist, Silver Spoon, and The Heroic Legend of Arslan... all of which received anime adaptations. Now, her latest series has been no different.

This is Yomi no Tsugai (Daemons of the Shadow Realm). Enough of the intro... Let’s Jam The Story Yuru is a boy working in a village all for the sake of his sister Asa, who, for some reason, is kept inside a cell with only a select few allowed to see her. Along for the ride is Yuru’s friend Danji, an energetic boy who doesn’t seem to be exceptional in anything that he does.

As Yuru is killing a pheasant for dinner, he looks up at a pair of chemtrails, thinking that it’s a dragon flying overhead. When he returns, a brilliant flash lights up the sky, and suddenly, the barrier protecting the village disappears. Military men storm the village, killing anyone and everything in their path as dual helicopters circle overhead, providing air support.

Then, a girl in a red trench coat shows up and mutters “Gobble” over and over again as people’s bodies are sliced in half effortlessly. Yuru’s grandmother knows that they are here for him and puts out the order to find and hide him, but it’s too late. A traveling merchant by the name of Dera is more than he seems. Once he sees the village getting attacked, he pulls out a cellphone and reports in on the situation. He storms the village, taking out as many soldiers as he can until he catches up with Yuru.

The grandmother instructs Dera to take him away and go into hiding. He obliges, but they run into a bit of an issue. He gives Yuru an amulet depicting the twin statues at the village’s front gates and tells him to slot it into the hole between them. When he does so, two yellow sentient pieces of energy rip apart the helicopters, later manifesting into a man and woman named Migi and Hidari (Right and Left).

They are Yuru’s Daemons! After the attack, Dera and Hana bring Yuru down the mountain and introduce him to the real world, which is a massive culture shock for him. Almost straight out of the gate, Yuru becomes hunted by members of the Kagemori Clan.

He winds up getting captured, only to discover that his real sister, Asa, is staying with them. Confused, Asa offers him an explanation, but it’s very hard for him to conceive that the Asa he visited back in the village was a fake all along. The Kagemoris have an interest in Yuru because he is the one prophesied to acquire the power of Seal, the other half of Asa’s Break; however, Dera tracks Yuru down and brings him back under his protection. Throughout it all, Yuru must track down information on his missing parents while unraveling the mystery of the various clans out there trying to capture him and Asa to acquire their powers.

All the while, the Higashi Clan and Kagemori Clan have to deal with their own internal problems as not all clans get along with their own members. Characters Yuru Yuru is our main protagonist, and even though he hasn’t awakened it yet, he is the one who is compatible with the power of Seal, one of the two legendary Daemons. His entire life was spent in Higashi village, isolated from the modern world.

Because of this, he only knows primitive skills such as hunting for his own food and surviving off the land. His mindset is noble, though, as he is very loyal to his village and to his friends. He would do anything to protect them, but he’s not a pushover by any means. His father always taught him to kill or be killed, and this is accentuated when he’s attacked by bandits and has to fend for his life. He recites the lessons his father told him before he and his mother took the real Asa and left the mountain, leaving him all by himself.

This creates his rough and gruff attitude while maintaining a kind heart because he understands the value of friends and family. He has an indirect comedic side when he’s introduced to the real world, as he has no clue about anything. He’s shocked he can buy meat at a store, doesn’t know what a phone is, and is even marveled that something as simple as aspirin is produced en masse and readily available. He’s a very balanced character!

Asa The one we met in the village was a doppelganger; however, the real Asa has one of the biggest brother complexes you will ever see. You would swear that she’s in love with Yuru; however, there is a moment during the show where she dreams of a normal life... which includes getting a boyfriend, so that throws that theory straight out of the window. Still, she obsesses over every little thing about Yuru, from the way he looks, to the sound of his voice, to the mere fact that he smiles at her, or even agrees to talk to her... she acts like it’s the biggest event in the world.

Outside of this, she’s very complex emotionally. After she was killed and forced to awaken Break, she has come to regret her isolated life, but she understands it’s for her own protection. Her dream is just to live a normal life with Yuru and her parents, but the fact that she can’t frustrates her. Still, she’s grateful to the Kagemori Clan for taking her in and protecting her, so she swears to use the power of Break to protect them, as it’s the least she can do to show that gratitude.

She can be quite annoying whenever Yuru’s around, but when she gets down and dirty, she is quite the force to be reckoned with... even if she can’t fully control Break just yet. Hidari and Migi Otherwise known as Right and Left, they are the Daemons that were encased in statues overseeing and protecting Higashi Village. Upon his escape with Dera, Yuru isn’t given much information, but is told to forge a contract with them by offering the statues his blood.

He does so, and they come to life. Apparently, they see Yuru as a kind master, and love the fact that Yuru will let them do as they please without much restriction. They are hard-headed, love to fight, and aren’t afraid of anything... mainly because their bodies are made of stone! They are excellent supporting characters for Yuru, who not only protect him, but also keep him in check from time to time as good guardians should! Dera Dera starts off as a traveling merchant who visits Higashi village.

Whenever he shows up, everyone is happy to see him, but that’s just a cover. His real mission is to watch over Yuru as a member of the Higashi Clan. When the village is attacked by the Kagemori Clan, he’s the one who helps Yuru escape and becomes his guardian in the real world. He’s also the one who helps form a kind of ceasefire pact with the Kagemori Clan and even enlists their help and vice versa from time to time as the Kagemori Clan deals with unrest from within their ranks.

Outside of being Yuru’s protector, he’s kind of a carefree goofball that doesn’t mind abusing Jin’s invitation to drink at his bar, or losing all of his money gambling on horse races. Despite his goofiness, when it comes to protecting Yuru, he is a top-notch combatant that knows how to use his head! Hana She is Dera’s partner in crime and also a member of the Higashi Clan.

Known as Gravedigger, she is usually summoned to clean up some of the Higashi’s Clan’s “messes” by disposing of their bodies. Because she knows the Higashi Clan also wants Break and Seal for themselves, she feigns ignorance when it comes to Yuru and Dera’s whereabouts, despite the fact that they are all living together in a hideout. She’s very short-tempered, finds kids highly annoying, and is constantly scolding Dera for squandering their savings on stupid stuff... especially when Dera ignores a lot of requests from the Higashi Clan, thus not earning any income. Despite her transgressions, she does have a heart, and though it is to her chagrin, she takes in Yuru... and others... along the way.

I can only see her as a comic relief type character, but there are some moments where she does play a bigger role. The fact that she is deceiving her own clan is rather odd, as it doesn’t really benefit her all that much, but she still does it for Yuru’s sake, if that tells you anything about the true nature of her character. The Kagemori Clan There are still a TON of characters to go, and some of these will dig a bit too deep into spoiler territory, so I’m going to lump them all together.

Gonzo Kagemori is the head of the clan, and he is about as kind as he is ruthless. He has a heart of gold and has zero problems taking strangers in and protecting them. In fact, a lot of the members of the Kagemori Clan are either orphans or people he came across who were down on their luck and needed a helping hand. His demons have the power to force other demons to coexist with one another, so he can make contracts with as many demons as he likes... which makes him terrifyingly powerful... almost at a legendary status amongst the clans. Just the mention of his name sends chills down anyone’s spine because of this.

He’s always happy, smiling, and very carefree... until you cross the clan... then, he is anything but. Friend, Family Member, Foe, or otherwise, he doesn’t care. The moment you attack the clan or betray them, it is an instant death sentence for you, showing his ruthless and cold side. If I’m being honest... he is my favorite character in the show.

He shows that the Kagemori Clan isn’t truly as evil as it seems, but because of his power and influence, it’s also a clan not to be taken lightly. His loyalty to his members is unmatched, but his punishment for those who betray that loyalty is something to be feared. It’s the perfect yin/yang combination, and there’s just something about him that just makes me love him as a character.

We have Jin Kagemori, one of Gonzo’s sons. Like Hana, he is the Kagemori Clan’s cleaner. He is very calm and mild-mannered, but he is also very apologetic and respectful when he knows there have been wrongs that need to be righted. Despite being from a different clan, and although he was a bit apprehensive at first, he works with Dera for the sake of the Kagemori Clan, showing that he is also analytical and calculated.

Above all else, you can tell he is loyal and trustworthy, but he also carries out Gonzo’s wishes without fail because he understands what it means to be for the Clan. If Gonzo suddenly wanted Dera killed, Jin would be the type of person to apologize to Dera for disposing of him. He is my second favorite character in the show!

Asuma is another one of Gonzo’s sons, but he seems the least trustworthy, and that’s because it’s his running gag. He doesn’t know how to smile properly, and because of that, he comes off as sly or scheming whenever he says anything. Many think he doesn’t mean what he says, or he’s just a snake, but the truth is, he does mean everything he says; he cares deeply and is also very loyal to the clan. Next we have Akio and Haruo Kuroya, as well as Gabby. All of them are orphans taken in by the Kagemori Clan.

While Akio and Haruo would go into spoilers, Gabby ends up befriending Asa to the point where she would do anything to protect her. Yes, she looks like a female Edward Elric, but she is a light tsundere character. She’s a firecracker when she wants to be, but she’s caring... especially with Asa. She’s tired of Asa always apologizing for things, so she literally kicks her rear whenever she does.

She seemed very evil at first during the Higashi Village attack, but she’s just another misunderstood character. Hikaru Kagemori is another one of Gonzo’s sons and is a pacifist. He wants to make manga and even teaches Asa how to draw to be one of his assistants.

He doesn’t agree with his father’s ruthlessness, and typically doesn’t involve himself in the family’s affairs. He just wants peace and quiet, but his demons can repair the manor whenever it’s damaged, so he’s quite useful in that regard because... yeah... the place gets torn up A LOT in this series. Danji We also have Danji... a super minor character at first who turns out to have a very significant role later. I’ll just say he’s Yuru’s best friend.

Shingo & Ivan The last ones I’ll touch on are Shingo and Ivan. Shingo is a man whose greed knows no bounds (where have we heard this before?). He wants to acquire Break and Seal for himself, and is one of the people causing problems for the Kagemori Clan.

Ivan is a hired mercenary who works under Shingo and is probably one of the most interesting characters in the series. He is a seriously skilled combatant with twin demon katanas... and to show off his power, he 1 v 4’s Yuru, Migi, Hidari, and Dera at the same time... and survives. He is set up to be one of the series’ main antagonists, and I just love his composure during battle plus his overall attitude. Needless to say, he’s my third favorite character! Yes, as much as I have spent here on the characters, there are still a TON of characters I didn’t mention, like Sakurazawa, the Kagemori Clan’s doctor, Yama the Shaman, Iori Shingo, Ken Tadera, Granny Yamaha, and all of the different demons throughout the world.

There is such a MASSIVE cast here to cover, but hopefully, I covered all the main and important ones. Art, Animation, and Sound Come on, guys... It’s bones. We already know it’s going to be good... and my God, is it good.

Despite having a massive cast of characters, every single one of them looked unique, distinct, and had their personalities shine through in their designs. From facial expressions to clothing, when you saw a character, you not only recognized who they were, but you already understood the type of character they would be. When you saw Jin, you knew he would be calm and collected, but someone not to mess with.

When you saw Shingo, you knew he was crazed and eccentric. When you saw Asa, you... okay... nothing could prepare you for the brother complex, but still... her design matches just how badass she is on the battlefield. The world itself was very well-crafted. From the stark differences of Higashi Village to the Modern World, nothing felt out of place.

Even with Higashi Village being stuck in the 1800s (or so), it still felt like a natural part of the world because of it being isolated in the mountains; its location made it believable that they would be cut off from everything, making Yuru’s confusion about modern technology and convenience valid. As far as the animation goes, it was also great. Every fight in this series absorbed you into the action, drew you into every movement, spell, and special effect.

Then again, as I said, this is bones we’re talking about here... they know how to deliver, and boy did they deliver. Even simple effects like a demon materializing looked so fluid and well pulled off. Most shows would have a PNG just fade in with an effect, but not here. These demons were fading in mid-animation... whether it’s riding on a magical horse or simply just walking. The level of detail and effort put in here was just top-notch.

Plus, the Ivan fight versus Left, Right, Yuru, and Dera was insane. They truly pulled off how skilled Ivan is, and it truly made you believe that this guy could be unkillable just from the animation alone. That’s not easy to do. As for sound?

The show’s soundtrack stood out well. It’s one of those that had excellent music to draw you into the action scenes, dark and brooding music during moments of drama, and then it had corny music during the comedic parts. Every part of the soundtrack was composed with the intention to get the most out of every scene.

Vaundy, which did a banger for The Summer Hikaru Died, was back for the first opening with Tobu Toki, and I thought it was the stronger of the two. That’s another thing... this show was 24 episodes long, and starting with Episode 13, we received a new opening for the show. Remember the times when anime would air for much longer than 12 or 13 episodes, and we always looked forward to the new opening? Yeah... that brought me back to when we swapped over to back shot by Masanori Otoda.

While that song was good in its own right, I still preferred Vaundy’s opening instead. Still, you can’t go wrong with either one, though. Overall Thoughts I don’t know what to say other than...

It’s Hiromu Arakawa. This is the fourth work of hers in a row to get adapted into an anime. The previous ones were Fullmetal Alchemist, Silver Spoon, and The Legend of Arslan... and the fact that she gets anime adaptations isn’t a fluke... It’s because she knows how to make an amazing story with character depth that stands the test of time. Arakawa is just a master at creating characters, and despite Daemons of the Shadow Realm having one of her biggest casts ever, you still feel the depth of her characters here.

Even supporting characters have tremendous depth and have a usefulness in the story. She makes you care about them as much as the story and world itself, and that is very, VERY hard to do consistently across multiple series, and yet, she pulls it off every single time. As I said above, the story is engaging, the fights are amazing, bones brought her work to life in ways that only they can, the music drove home every moment, and everything felt as cohesive as ever. The ONLY complaint that I would have is that the series ended on a cliffhanger without a definitive conclusion, but that can be forgiven because as soon as the final episode aired, it was announced that Daemons of the Shadow Realm was receiving a second season, so we’re not done yet!

I am not sure if Season 2 will also have 24 episodes, but with how much I enjoyed this show, I sure hope that it does! Whether you have seen any of Arakawa’s previous works or not, if you just want an amazing shonen battle anime to sink your teeth into with actual depth in its story and characters, then you cannot go wrong with Daemons of the Shadow Realm. Simply put... watch this show!

Overall Score: 4.5 / 5 Daemons of the Shadow Realm Daemons of the Shadow Realm is the latest work from Hiromu Arakawa about a boy named Yuru who has only known an isolated life in a small village. After an attack, he escapes the mountain and must face the modern world, find his lost parents, and avoid being hunted by clans who want his unawakened power... all while learning to deal with the Daemons and their masters. Pros Great story In-depth characters Thrilling action Excellent animation and effects Cons I can’t really think of many flaws outside of the comedy being a little too over-the-top at times. Overall 4.5

cae0d72c-975d-4ebe-b07b-2bfbbd8c0db5.title: I Love Justin Hartley’s Comments On Jensen Ackles’ Tracker Season 4 Return, But What About Melissa Roxburgh?
cae0d72c-975d-4ebe-b07b-2bfbbd8c0db5.incipit: (Image credit: Darko Sikman/CBS, Darko Sikman/CBS, Sergei Bachlakov/CBS) Tracker is gearing up for Season 4 amid the 2026 TV schedule, and there is much to be excited about. For one, Jensen Ackles will...
cae0d72c-975d-4ebe-b07b-2bfbbd8c0db5.body:
(Image credit: Darko Sikman/CBS, Darko Sikman/CBS, Sergei Bachlakov/CBS) Tracker is gearing up for Season 4 amid the 2026 TV schedule , and there is much to be excited about. For one, Jensen Ackles will once again be returning as Russell Shaw, the brother of Justin Hartley 's Colter, after taking on some shady work to protect him. Hartley shared what’s in store for Ackles’ return, and, as pumped as I am, I’m still wondering where Melissa Roxburgh stands and whether she'll return as Colter and Russell's sister, Dory.

What Justin Hartley Said About Jensen Ackles’ Return Ackles made his first appearance as Colter’s estranged brother in the first season. Since then, the two have slowly repaired their relationship while learning more about their late father. The two siblings even worked on some cases together (with varied results). Despite his busy schedule and working on The Boys prequel, Vought Rising , Ackles will indeed be back for Season 4.

Not only that, but he’ll be appearing early in the season, as Hartley confirmed to TV Insider : Well, right now he is about probably 100 meters away from me. He’s in at least one [episode], and we’ll have him back when we can. I think probably in the new year, we’ll have him back for a few.

I love that even though Ackles is so busy with other projects, he’s still trying to come back to Tracker when he can, and the producers are making sure that happens. It’s been fun to see Colter and Russell’s dynamic, especially since Hartley and Ackles are longtime pals . Knowing that Ackles might even be back for the latter half of Season 4 is making me curious as to what could be in store. As for this first appearance in the upcoming season, Russell is going to be reaching out for his brother’s help. Hartley explained: What’s he been up to is he won’t tell me.

Well, he kind of can’t, right? I mean, there’s a quid pro quo thing that happened at the end of Season 3, and he’s like, ‘As long as my brother doesn’t find out about this, I’ll do this thing for you.' But when we find him and when he reaches out to Colter, he needs help with something. One of his buddies is in dire straits, big time dire straits — and not a self-inflicted thing, just sort of something that happened to him, and he thinks of his brother Colter, and he’s like, ‘I bet you Colter can help you with this.’ So, he reaches out and of course Colter’s willing to help and it reunites the two brothers and they go on this pretty epic journey. Even though Russell is clearly keeping something from Colter, I like that he still feels the need to reach out for help.

It's hard to predict what will happen when the Shaw brothers get together, and I can only assume that whatever Russell is hiding will eventually come to light. For now, though, their relationship seems to be unchanged. The more they get together, though, the more I wonder about their sister.

What's Going On With Melissa Roxburgh? Roxburgh guest starred in Tracker ’s first season as Colter and Russell’s sister, Dr. Dory Shaw. So far, that’s been her only appearance.

Of course, Roxburgh was busy with her show, The Hunting Party , which was unfortunately canceled after two seasons on NBC . Now that her schedule is a bit more open, could we be seeing Dory in the near-future? Hartley weighed in on the possibility, and he’s keeping an open mind: It’s possible.

All these people that I thought, what a great idea to have on the show, they’re all so damn busy now, right? It’s not a secret that they’re all really good, so they’re all working a lot. So, anything’s possible. We’ll see. Ever since Season 1, I have wanted nothing more than to have all three Shaw siblings on screen together.

As for how the show could bring back Dory, I’m not sure. I think the logical route would be to bring her into a story involving the trio's dad, and perhaps that could connect to what Russell is hiding from Colter. As of now, Roxburgh doesn't seem to be attached to any projects since The Hunting Party , but it’s possible she’s still working on something that's just yet to it be announced. I'll certainly maintain optimism about Melissa Roxburgh returning to Tracker .

But, for now, I'll just be grateful that Justin Hartley and Jensen Ackles will get to share the screen more. Check out Season 4, which premieres on Sunday, October 4 at 9:30 p.m. ET on CBS.

The show will then move to its regular time slot of 9 p.m. ET the following week. Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News Passionate writer. Obsessed with anything and everything entertainment, specifically movies and television.

Can get easily attached to fictional characters.

a73945f3-1268-4cba-9efb-525407e9cbbe.incipit: With several new faces and the fifth-youngest opening night roster in the NHL, the St. Louis Blues will look quite different when they take the ice in Dallas on Friday. a73945f3-1268-4cba-9efb-525407e9cbbe.body:
With several new faces and the fifth-youngest opening night roster in the NHL, the St. Louis Blues will look quite different when they take the ice in Dallas on Friday. So will the way fans watch them this season.

For years, the Blues aired the majority of their games through a traditional regional sports network. That model, however, has largely unraveled across professional sports, with the collapse of FanDuel Sports Network parent company Main Street Sports Group as just one example. The team now enters the 2026-27 season with Blue Note+, a new team-owned television package that Chris Zimmerman, president and CEO of Blues business operations, says gives the franchise greater control over how its games are produced, distributed, and sold to advertisers. Are you a CITY SC fan?

Subscribe to the CITY Scene newsletter to get a fan’s guide to the pro soccer scene in St. Louis. We will never send spam or annoying emails.

Unsubscribe anytime. This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google Privacy Policy and Terms of Service apply. For fans, the important part is much simpler. Blues games that last season aired locally on FanDuel Sports Network will now be found on Blue Note+, with several options for tuning in. The network will be available through services such as Spectrum and Fubo, and fans can also subscribe to Blue Note+ through Amazon Prime Video for either $19.99 per month or $99.99 annually.

A Prime membership is not required. The team isn’t done adding ways to watch. During a media event Tuesday at Enterprise Center, Blues executive vice president and chief revenue and marketing officer Steve Chapman said he believes the Blues are “inside the 10-yard line” on a distribution agreement with DirecTV. If completed, the agreement would cover DirecTV, DirecTV Stream, and U-verse TV.

“Deal’s not done,” Chapman said, “but we’re certainly working towards it.” Comcast, meanwhile, represents another significant piece of the distribution puzzle that the team’s business office is still working to solve. What to expect The changes don’t stop at where fans will find the games. By taking control of their local broadcasts, the Blues will have more freedom to experiment this season with how their games look and sound.

You may notice these tweaks in ways both big and small. Blues play-by-play voice Chris Kerber said the St. Louis Cardinals’ broadcasts this past season serve as an example. With Cardinals.TV , a direct-to-consumer streaming service produced in partnership with Major League Baseball, the Cardinals were able to incorporate their own production ideas that gave broadcasts a different feel than previous years, including a cable-suspended camera that could move along the baseline of Busch Stadium, Kerber says.

The Blues have similar ideas for this season. Kerber said two camera positions that had disappeared from Blues broadcasts in recent years will return this season. The angles may not be immediately obvious to viewers, he added, but they’ll give the production crew more angles to work with on replays and when breaking down a play.

Blue Note Productions, the team’s in-house content crew, will also have a greater role in the broadcasts, bringing the storytelling they already produce to television. That freedom to expand and enhance the broadcast options comes with a learning curve. Where some production decisions used to be dictated by a regional sports network, the Blues can make more of those calls themselves. “We’re going to learn, we’re going to stumble at times, we’re going to make some mistakes,” Zimmerman said. “But I really believe the ultimate result is more energy around St.

Louis Blues hockey. That’s ultimately what we’re here for.” Different kinds of suites The Blues are also rethinking what a luxury suite at Enterprise Center should look like—and who it can serve. New this year are the Studio Suites, a fresh spin on the arena’s traditional luxury boxes. Located inside the Bommarito Lounge, Studio Suites are designed for small groups in a more open, shared environment with all-inclusive food and drinks.

Part of the idea is to reach companies—particularly small and mid-size businesses—that want to entertain clients and employees without having to fill a larger suite every game. “It’s essentially a semi-private suite area,” said John Alvarado, the Blues’ manager of premium events and suite sales. “Companies may not want to host 12 to 16 people every game, but they do want to entertain six to eight-ish people.” Nick Wierciak, vice president of ticketing, premium and suite sales, said the concept also reflects changing tastes among customers.

“I think people are less interested in private and stuffy, and more interested in an open concept,” Wierciak said. The Studio Suites replace the area where the pre-, post-, and intermission television reports were set during previous seasons. Those segments will now be shot live mere steps away in the area formerly known as the Bud Light Sports Pub. That bar is getting a makeover and new Anheuser-Busch branding focused on Michelob Ultra.

How about some hockey? Of course, none of the changes will matter much if the Blues don’t carry their end of the bargain on the ice. After finishing four points shy of the final wild card spot last season—and missing the playoffs for the third time in four seasons—the Blues are hopeful they’ve done enough this offseason to return to the tournament.

Others are less bullish. A preseason panel of 14 NHL.com writers and editors, for example, aren’t sold on the Blues’ upside. Only two picked St. Louis to squeak into a Western Conference wild card slot. Blues analyst Joey Vitale says he expects this year’s group will need to establish an identity in the defensive zone, pointing to the Blues’ premium goaltending tandem of Joel Hofer and Jordan Binnington and the arrival of new assistant coach Greg Cronin, whom Vitale believes will reinforce an emphasis on defending and attention to detail.

“For you fans coming to the game, is it going to be 7-6 affairs? I don’t think so,” Vitale says. “I think they’re going to have to win games 2-1, 3-2, 1-0 and squeeze it out in overtime like we’ve seen.”

2976dbc3-0f9c-44de-8374-e746508f0a45.title: Strictly Come Dancing review – delighted new hosts helps show feel genuinely fresh
2976dbc3-0f9c-44de-8374-e746508f0a45.incipit: At this point, Strictly Come Dancing cannot be allowed to fail. When we’re all living off our Wes Streeting-mandated prepper rations, it’s the only thing that will keep us going, linking us to a time when...
2976dbc3-0f9c-44de-8374-e746508f0a45.body:
At this point, Strictly Come Dancing cannot be allowed to fail. When we’re all living off our Wes Streeting-mandated prepper rations, it’s the only thing that will keep us going, linking us to a time when joy, sparkle and diversity brought the nation together. Enshittification stalks the show – it has long felt too repetitive, its celeb lineups seem to get feebler each year, and the departure of longstanding presenters Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman threatened to be a lethal blow – so there’s a lot riding on this new series.

“Strictly Come Dancing – still fabulous,” said the continuity announcer introducing the launch show, not sounding entirely sure. On early impressions, it just might be. The new presenters Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe and Johannes Radebe look not a little terrified, but the vibe they’re going for is can’t-quite-believe-we-got-the-gig humility combined with superfan credentials, which is absolutely the right note. In all the shots of them watching the action – the pro dancers’ routine, the return of last year’s winner, former footballer Karen Carney – they look so thrilled it’s endearing.

The launch show is often tedious – not much dancing and not much from the judges. Photograph: Guy Levy/BBC/PA “It’s a little bit overwhelming to be here, but we are so delighted,” says Widdicombe, following the brilliant opening number. It’s an “honour”, coos Willis, who also says she feels as if she should be curtsying when the judges enter.

Radebe, until now one of the show’s professional dancers, brings some elegant restraint. He may not have their presenting experience, but he’s not as dazzled by the glitter as his co-hosts. The launch show is always tedious – not much dancing, not much from the judges and gnawing irritation at all the “celebrities” you’ve never heard of – but you get the sense they’re all giving it everything. Everyone laughs a bit too hard, previous series are heavily referenced, and the word “journey” is mentioned more times than I care to hear it. Not much can be done at this stage, barring some minor injuries, about this year’s pitiful celebrity lineup – a fact that will, unfortunately, become even more dazzling when the BBC’s new favourite show, Celebrity Traitors, starts again in a few weeks – though at least, unlike the year before last, there’s nobody who is famous for being in an advert.

The pro dancers must now be better-known than some of their celebrity partners, including a reality TV star (Love Island winner Cach Mercer), a TV presenter (Will Best from Big Brother, but not even the good Channel 4 version) and more than a few others to which the response can only be “no, me neither”. There are five new pro dancers for this series, and a new way of setting up the couples. Photograph: Guy Levy/BBC/PA There are some gems, among them Dame Sarah Storey, Britain’s most successful Paralympian, former footballer Shaun Wright-Phillips and actor Jaime Winstone. Still, Strictly has always been greater than the sum of its stars, and so it keeps hoofing along.

It’s been rocked by affairs and accusations of bullying, but it’s also been a rare refuge of joy and progress. Actor Bethany Antonia – familiar to anyone who watches HBO’s House of the Dragon – grew up with Strictly, now in its 22nd year, and tells her fellow contestants that watching boxer Nicola Adams dance with Katya Jones in the show’s first same-sex pairing in 2020 “was such a big part of my coming out journey”, encouraged, she says, by watching the positive reaction of her family every Saturday night. Antonia gets to dance with Nancy Xu, and they both look ecstatic to have been given each other, though this is also the default setting of every pairing.

Nobody is allowed to look disappointed. There are five new pro dancers for this series, and a new way of setting up the couples, which is, as everyone keeps saying, a bit like speed-dating – they keep swapping partners, brave for a show which has been blamed for many a ruined marriage, until a couple is called. It’s only slightly less dull than the old way. Strictly has always been greater than the sum of its stars.

Photograph: Guy Levy/BBC/PA So the couples are set (it’s Winstone and last year’s pro winner Carlos Gu all the way for me), and the new presenters have had their soft launch – this show is pre-recorded, but from now on it will be live – and although I’m not convinced it takes three, the signs are good. Willis is a class act, Widdicombe is best when he’s given the space to gently rib the contestants and Radebe brings such an air of gentle benevolence to otherwise shouty primetime TV it feels genuinely fresh. Maybe I just really want it to work.

74fdc203-1fed-41ef-974a-10773ec4b47c.title: LETTERS | DStv drops the ball in package overhaul
74fdc203-1fed-41ef-974a-10773ec4b47c.incipit: DStv’s pricing “reforms” have not delivered genuine affordability. Premium sports rugby, F1 and cricket remain locked behind top-tier packages while the rest of the schedule is padded with repeats and old...
74fdc203-1fed-41ef-974a-10773ec4b47c.body:
DStv’s pricing “reforms” have not delivered genuine affordability. Premium sports rugby, F1 and cricket remain locked behind top-tier packages while the rest of the schedule is padded with repeats and old movies that add little value. Renaming or restructuring packages means little if the underlying content mix stays the same.

The business model itself looks increasingly unsustainable. Advertising revenue alone cannot justify keeping flagship sports siloed on premium tiers while other sporting codes are scattered across lower packages. This fragmentation forces subscribers to pay for multiple tiers just to follow the sports they care about. There’s also a structural gap in how packages are designed.

DStv should offer genuinely separate offerings for South African subscribers versus international viewers, rather than a one-size-fits-all pricing structure that serves neither market well. Regulatory oversight has been largely absent. The Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (Icasa) has done little to address DStv’s dominant position in the pay-TV market, leaving consumers with few real alternatives.

Meanwhile, the SABC has failed to build the kind of compelling content that could offer genuine competition, leaving a vacuum DStv has exploited for years. The frustration is understandable: many South Africans feel they’re paying premium prices for a service that doesn’t reflect global standards and are questioning whether continuing to subscribe or turning to alternatives is the only leverage consumers have left. South Africa deserves a pay-TV market with real competition, transparent pricing and regulators willing to act. Until that happens, subscriber frustration will keep growing. — Burton Brown, Gqeberha ANC plus SAPS equals disaster When South African law enforcement agencies joined a shocked nation in search of a possible serial killer prowling around Kempton Park, one couldn’t stop thinking about how the ANC has destroyed the SAPS. The damage control was left to a silver-tongued spokeswoman, but her eloquence couldn’t paper over the terrible reality that criminals have now become audacious, vicious and totally inhumane.

The enabling environment was created by none other than the ANC, the reckless implementation of affirmative action, poorly trained and vetted police officers and the appointment of ANC loyalists to senior positions. But the most treasonous is the abuse of the slush funds to fight factional battles. When this was happening, local and international crime syndicates were identifying our country as a playground. Gender-based violence is a component of an uncontrolled crime calamity besieging our country, with over 23,000 murders a year, fuelled partly by an abandoned youth. — Mishack Nthane, by e-mail GBV is the problem of all men There’s no need for a thesis, conferences, press releases, speeches, strategies, blueprints or best practice.

The solution is very simple: gender-based violence will only end when men take collective responsibility for the actions of other men. It is not enough to simply not be violent; true protection requires active peer intervention. If every single man ensures that just one other man in his circle does not harm or abuse a woman, the network of violence collapses.

We must break the silence of brotherhood and hold each other accountable. The burden of safety belongs on the shoulders of men, not the lives of women. — Grant Son, by e-mail Jail Daybreak Foods crooks Reading the report of the latest disclosures about events at Daybreak Foods and the Public Investment Corporation (PIC), your first feeling is that it cannot be true. Yet, there it stands in black and white: “The DA has lodged a formal complaint with the Legal Practice Council (LPC) against attorney Pulane Jimmy Malahlela and Malahlela & Company Attorneys over extraordinary legal spending at Daybreak Foods ...” The disclosures that the collapsed poultry company paid more than R124m to a single law firm potentially confirm a deep-seated suspicion raised long ago by the Association for Monitoring and Advocacy of Government Pensions that the company was used as a convenient conduit to channel public funds elsewhere. This shows all the signs of calculated, large-scale plundering.

What makes this crisis scandalous is the source of the money. Daybreak Foods is owned by the PIC on behalf of the Government Employees Pension Fund, the Unemployment Insurance Fund and the Compensation Fund. The findings of forensic investigations that nearly R40m in legal expenses cannot be linked to invoices at all and that millions were made in duplicate payments indicate nothing less than a national disgrace.

There must be serious consequences for offenders, and the money must be recovered. While a single law firm allegedly lined its pockets at the expense of the public, the disastrous collapse of Daybreak Foods caused nearly 1,900 innocent workers to lose their jobs. Furthermore, the National Council of Societies for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals had to euthanise hundreds of thousands of starving chickens due to a feed shortage. This illustrates the devastating human and moral cost of these events. The DA’s formal complaint to the LPC against Malahlela and Co is a necessary first step, but it cannot stop there.

This is now undoubtedly a matter for the Hawks and the Special Investigating Unit. It must be determined exactly where these millions flowed and who the ultimate beneficiaries of this plundering were. People who are guilty of malpractice or crime must be prosecuted and placed behind bars. The time for talking is over; the people of South Africa must demand that their hard-earned money be recovered. — Adamus P Stemmet, Ridgeworth Mapisa-Nqakula’s claims not credible I’ve followed the corruption and money-laundering case of former defence minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula with some interest.

The trial is currently postponed due to the former minister once again apparently taking ill — something that seems to occur with rather too much frequency these days among her set facing similar charges. Mapisa-Nqakula’s claims that she’s “not an EFT person” are simply not credible. I know this woman well.

Neither is her insistence on using a court interpreter when her English language skills are on a par with mine. It seems to be another ploy in the dock to buy her time to think about her answers before giving them. She is a highly intelligent, capable and manipulative individual. She’s also a liar and a thief.

And yes, you may quote me. She claims that much of the cash appearing in her bank account is from “foreign travel savings”, which is again neither credible nor accurate. I think what she means is that taxpayers’ funding of her daily allowances for all her overseas ministerial junkets has been converted from US dollars to rands and then pocketed.

That’s not “savings”, and certainly not savings for the taxpayers who funded her foreign junkets. /.I strongly suspect she has been claiming the maximum daily US dollar allowance and then not spending it. Why would she? She was the minister, and everything was already paid for. Instead of returning the unspent US dollars she kept them for herself, converted them to rands and pocketed the cash. I suspect she’s far from being the only one who’s done this.

Are ministers’ foreign travel accounts not audited? There’s also the big question of why she was overseas in the first place. Where? Doing what?

What benefit to South Africa for each multimillion-rand ministerial overseas visit with flunkies and officials along for the ride? Except to accumulate more cash “savings” for her home-building operations. — Mark Lowe, Durban

a44174a6-cf59-4010-b93d-f329d3182b86.title: ‘Wait, what?’ Jimmy Fallon stunned as Houston reporter Lauren Kelly reveals her Beyoncé connection
a44174a6-cf59-4010-b93d-f329d3182b86.incipit: Houston TV correspondent Lauren Kelly surprised Jimmy Fallon with her 1995 yearbook, revealing she went to middle school with Beyoncé and Kelly Rowland.Jimmy Fallon was stunned when Lauren Kelly revealed that...
a44174a6-cf59-4010-b93d-f329d3182b86.body:
Houston TV correspondent Lauren Kelly surprised Jimmy Fallon with her 1995 yearbook, revealing she went to middle school with Beyoncé and Kelly Rowland. Jimmy Fallon was stunned when Lauren Kelly revealed that she went to middle school with Beyoncé and Kelly Rowland. (Instagram / Getty Images) Jimmy Fallon was expecting a conversation about the new season of The Tonight Show. Instead, Houston TV correspondent Lauren Kelly arrived with a piece of local history that left the late-night host visibly surprised.

Houston TV host reveals her big Beyonce connection to Jimmy Fallon Lauren Kelly, a correspondent for KPRC 2’s Houston Life, travelled to New York City and interviewed Fallon inside The Tonight Show studio at Rockefeller Cent re on Thursday. The conversation covered the NBC programme’s new season and Fallon’s previous visit to Houston, but it was Kelly’s old school yearbook that quickly became the standout moment. Kelly brought her 1995 middle school yearbook with her. Inside were photographs of two classmates who would go on to become major names in music: Beyoncé Knowles and Kelly Rowland.

Fallon’s reaction was immediate. “Wait, what?” he said, before asking Kelly, “You went to school with Beyoncé?” Kelly confirmed that she had, explaining that both Beyoncé and Rowland were already singing at the time. She recalled the pair as “the most fantastic people, the most talented and down-to-earth people”.

The revelation gave the interview an unexpected Houston connection. Kelly was not simply talking about Beyoncé as a global superstar looking back at her early years; she was sharing memories from a time when the singer was still a schoolgirl in Houston. Jimmy's reaction to the yearbook pictures The yearbook quickly became the centre of the conversation, with Fallon eager to see the photographs for himself. Kelly showed him the pages featuring Beyoncé and Rowland, giving him a glimpse of the future stars before their careers had taken them around the world. Fallon then turned his attention to Kelly’s own photograph.

He asked to see her yearbook picture as well, prompting Kelly to joke about her 1995 appearance. “Please give me a little bit of slack because this was before any hair products in 1995,” Kelly said. The exchange added a more personal note to the interview, turning an ordinary television appearance into a trip back through Kelly’s school days. The Houston connection also extended beyond Beyoncé.

During the conversation, Fallon looked back on his own visit to Houston and remembered the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo, including trying his hand at roping cattle and enjoying Texas barbecue. Kelly’s encounter with Fallon comes as The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon enters a new season, with NBC promoting new sketches, celebrity appearances and other surprises. KPRC 2 reported that Kelly was invited to sit in the studio seat that has hosted some of the programme’s biggest guests.

Before joining Livemint, Trisha worked with India Today as an entertainment journalist and film critic. There, she reviewed films, covered industry news, and built a strong foundation in storytelling and cultural analysis. <br> Trisha enjoys working at the intersection of media, culture, and audience interest, always looking for fresh angles and formats.

Films, shows, and music are not just her beat but her biggest passion — something that naturally reflects in her writing. Whether it’s cinema, streaming shows, music, or internet trends, she approaches every story with curiosity and intent. <br> Outside the job description, she’s unapologetically passionate about films, shows, and music — sometimes a little too passionate, if you ask her. That enthusiasm often spills into her work, adding personality, urgency, and a touch of chaos that keeps her writing alive.

b8ec904e-9399-4d4a-a93a-48019b7d3f79.title: Strictly returns with new hosting trio as celebrities find out dance pairings
b8ec904e-9399-4d4a-a93a-48019b7d3f79.incipit: Strictly returns with new hosting trio as celebrities find out dance pairings2 hours agoFreya Scott-TurnerBBC/PAStrictly Come Dancing has returned to the small screen for its 24th series, in a new era for the...
b8ec904e-9399-4d4a-a93a-48019b7d3f79.body:
Strictly returns with new hosting trio as celebrities find out dance pairings 2 hours ago Freya Scott-Turner BBC/PA Strictly Come Dancing has returned to the small screen for its 24th series, in a new era for the show as it moves forward with a revamped presenting line up. Broadcaster Emma Willis, comedian Josh Widdicombe and former Strictly professional Johannes Radebe made their presenting debut on Saturday, taking over from long-running hosting duo Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman, who left the show last year. A fresh cohort of famous faces – including actress Melanie Walters and former England footballer Shaun Wright-Phillips – also stepped onto the ballroom floor for the first time.

During the launch show, it was revealed which professional dancers they were paired with. Stepping out onto the ballroom floor after a huge all-cast opening dance routine, Willis said presenting Strictly was a "genuine honour". "Josh, you've got moves," proclaimed Radebe, a former professional on the show. While Widdicombe added that it was "a little bit overwhelming" but he was "delighted" to be there.

In a first for the show, celebrity and pro pairings were revealed via three dance routines. It functioned as a musical chairs of sorts, in which the contestants switched partners until the music was paused, and a couple was announced. BBC/PA Strictly contestants 2026 Here is a list of the pairings in full: Actress Lacey Turner and Vito Coppola Reality TV star Dani Dyer and Nikita Kuzmin Hair stylist to the stars Chris Appleton and Amy Dowden Australian singer and actress Delta Goodrem and Kai Widdrington DJ and social media personality Cach Mercer and Maddie Ingoldsby TV and radio presenter Will Best and Dianne Buswell Paralympian Dame Sarah Storey and Julian Caillon Actress Jaime Winstone and Carlos Gu TV and stage actress Bethany Antonia and Nancy Xu Former England footballer Shaun Wright-Phillips and Alexis Warr Presenter and author Graeme Hall and Lauren Oakley Actor Lawrence Robb and Jowita Przystał Skeleton athlete Tabby Stoecker and Mark Karmalita YouTuber John Nellis and Katya Jones TV and stage actress Melanie Walters and Aljaž Škorjanec One pair who won't need to get to know each other are reality TV star Dani Dyer and Nikita Kuzmin.

Dyer is back to compete for a second time, having withdrawn from last year's series due to a fractured ankle. "I'm just over the moon. I'm so, so happy," she said after the pairing, while Kuzmin added that he had "tears of joy" in his eyes. Meanwhile, actress Bethany Antonia and professional Nancy Xu became the third two-woman couple to compete in the show. In a poignant moment, Antonia revealed that watching boxer Nicola Adams and Katya Jones performing together in Strictly's 2020 series was a "big part of my coming out journey".

Among the other pairings were EastEnders actress Lacey Turner and Vito Coppola, former Paralympian Dame Sarah Storey and Julian Caillon, and Shaun Wright-Phillips and Alexis Warr. Also back on the dancefloor for a final spin was reigning Strictly champion, former Lionness Karen Carney. Clad in the same diamante-encrusted football shirt, Carney recreated the Jive that first marked her out as a contender of her series, alongside dance partner Carlos Gu. "I absolutely feel like I'm at home," Carney told Willis after the routine, as she paid tribute to her pro partner.

In 13 weeks time, she'll have to surrender that glitterball trophy to a new victor. BBC/PA Reigning champion Karen Carney returned to perform her week one Jive with pro partner Carlos Gu And it is not just presenters and celebrities navigating the ballroom for the first time: Aleksandra Isaeva, Cristian Priori, Lethabo Monametsi, Maddie Ingoldsby, and Mark Karmalita are the five new professionals joining the Strictly cast this series. They hail from the UK, Canada, Italy, South Africa and Ukraine.

The five made a high-impact entrance, performing a searing routine that kicked off on top of an enormous encaged disco ball. BBC/PA Strictly's five new professional dancers gave a high-octane debut performance Saturday's show was a more paired back role for Craig Revel Horwood and his fellow judges - Motsi Mabuse, Shirley Ballas and Anton Du Beke - who featured less. But there was still time for resident villain Horwood to direct a jibe at broadcaster Will Best's hip action: "Call in the paramedics darling, dislocation - my goodness." And some other traditions remain intact. Once all the dance routines were wrapped, the pairings announced, and the chats in the "Clauditorium" concluded, it was time for the show's three new hosts to bid farewell with the customary order to "staaart dancing!"

aafce2ac-498d-4152-a663-f94cf6b730c1.title: Charlie Sheen and dad Martin reunite for 'wonderful' family comedy
aafce2ac-498d-4152-a663-f94cf6b730c1.incipit: Charlie Sheen is teaming up with his father Martin Sheen for a new sitcom. The 61-year-old star and his 86-year-old actor dad will reunite on screen for AMC's upcoming family comedy Happy Jack, which is set to be filmed at Warner Bros Studios ahead of a six-episode run in 2027. The logline for the series reads: "Charli
aafce2ac-498d-4152-a663-f94cf6b730c1.body:
Charlie Sheen is teaming up with his father Martin Sheen for a new sitcom. The 61-year-old star and his 86-year-old actor dad will reunite on screen for AMC's upcoming family comedy Happy Jack, which is set to be filmed at Warner Bros Studios ahead of a six-episode run in 2027. The logline for the series reads: "Charlie Sheen plays Jack, a bit of a lifelong ne'er-do-well.

"He's got two great daughters (though his Dad, played by Martin Sheen, deserves more credit for how they turned out). "Kate runs Jack's company and keeps him on the rails while Sam is a wild child who is more like her Dad. "When Sam comes home to introduce everyone to her new boyfriend, Jack's shocked to learn Paul, a former investment banker turned van life guru, is the same age as he is. "Shocked at first (hypocrisy be damned), Jack soon realises he's got a choice to make.

Will he keep looking out for number one, or embrace this last chance to be a real part of his daughters' lives?" The show has former Two And A Half Men pair Jim Patterson and Matt Ross on board as writers, co-showrunners, and executive producers. Charlie said in a statement: "I've always heard the moments that truly matter happen when they're supposed to. "The good folks at AMC have played a huge hand in deciding that moment is now.

"It's no secret that it's been a minute, and I'm thrilled to be going back on television in such a meaningful way in an equally wonderful show. "The crew has reassembled – suffice it to say, it's time to give the people what they want." Martin previously made a guest appearance alongside his son in Two And A Half Men, while he also played Charlie's character's dad in Anger Management. The real life father-and-son duo had the same relationship in Wall Street and No Code of Conduct, while other projects they've shared include Cadence, Free Money and Hot Shots Part Deux. Dan McDermott, chief content officer of AMC Global Media and president of AMC Studios, added: "What a thrill to welcome Charlie Sheen and Martin Sheen to AMC and AMC+, playing a father and son in this original family comedy, Happy Jack. "I worked with Charlie years ago on Spin City and he is a singular talent who has owned the screen in some of the most unforgettable films and television series ever made.

"We love this show from a great creative team, led by Jim Patterson and Matt Ross, and the Tannenbaums."

efbbe9d0-f0e7-43f1-90ac-ad872579c50c.title: ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Creator Reacts to Netflix Cancellation: ‘I Hope Serenity Will Always Have a Place in Your Heart’
efbbe9d0-f0e7-43f1-90ac-ad872579c50c.incipit: Following the news that “Sweet Magnolias” has been canceled at Netflix, creator and showrunner Sheryl J. Anderson is looking back on the romantic drama’s 5 Season run. “Living in Serenity for five seasons...
efbbe9d0-f0e7-43f1-90ac-ad872579c50c.body:
Following the news that “ Sweet Magnolias ” has been canceled at Netflix , creator and showrunner Sheryl J. Anderson is looking back on the romantic drama’s 5 Season run. “Living in Serenity for five seasons has been a privilege and a blessing,” Anderson shared in the caption of an Instagram post Saturday.

“The people I’ve met and worked with — our incredible writers, cast, crew, executives, and producers — have touched my heart and changed my life.” She continued: “And our fans have been amazing in their passion for our characters. Thank you all. Though our journey has sadly come to an end, I hope Serenity will always have a place in your heart. Keep pouring it out!” The Netflix show first premiered on the platform in May 2020, and starred JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Brooke Elliott and Heather Headley.

Originally adapted from the book series by New York Times best-selling author Sherryl Woods, the streamer announced that the show continuously ranked among Netflix’s Global Top 10 in over 60 countries after announcing its return for a fifth season in 2025. The “comfort drama,” as described by Netflix, followed the lifelong friendship between Maddie (Swisher), Dana Sue (Elliott), and Helen (Headley) “as they juggle relationships, family and careers in the charming small town of Serenity, S.C.” Though “Sweet Magnolias” may be coming to an end, Netflix announced that Swisher and Anderson would be teaming for a new drama series titled “Ladies of the House.” Variety previously reported that Anderson will serve as showrunner, with Swisher potentially starring and executive producing with Kate Gordon under their Rolling Clover banner, alongside executive producers at Black Label Media. The logline reads, “When the charismatic owner of a winery dies unexpectedly, his wife and two adult daughters must battle through their issues with each other in order to confront challenges with the business, their extended family, and the men in their lives.

Good friends and good wine will aid in the journey to hang on to the winery, but what matters most is that they find a way to hang on to each other.”
